tspan.tspan: A river is usually modeled as a closed system, with the bed constituting the bottom boundary of
the domain. However, when the bed is porous, the hyporheic (subsurface) flow exchanges

text.tspan: momentum with the main flow and governs the velocity profile.

tspan.tspan: Building on established empirical
relationships that illustrate the velocity
profile of the main flow, we aim to
By closing the Reynolds and
dispersive
stresses, along with the drag force
density for flows over porous beds
(Rousseau & Ancey, 2022), one can derive
the one-dimensional momentum
equation governing the vertical velocity
profile. A numerical solver is then
implemented to compare the solution

text.tspan: with the existing empirical friction laws.

tspan.tspan: Because the bed has an irregular shape and disrupts the
uniformity of the flow, we need to observe
the flow at a scale
larger than the particle size. We perform
a spatial average
over a representative elementary volume (REV) to enable the
inclusion of porosity effects in the Navier-
Stokes equations
(Nikora, 2001). An additional stress, known as dispersive
stress, emerges. This stress was calibrated with a small-scale
experiment (image on the right ; Gauthier & Ancey, 2022) as a

text.tspan: mixing length with a single parameter λ = 0.015.

tspan.tspan: By converting our second-order ordinary differential equation into a
linearized partial differential equation (by adding a residual), we can

text.tspan: use the finite element method to solve the equation numerically.

tspan.tspan: At the bottom boundary, a simple Darcy velocity is set,
while the top

text.tspan: boundary is left free of any traction.

tspan.tspan: The numerical solution accurately represents the overall behavior of very shallow flows,
with the parameter
λ
adjusted to 0.3 to align with the established empirical laws in the
limit of deep flow, where
h / d
p
. The high value of the parameter
λ
relatively to its

text.tspan: experimental value of 0.015) highlights the important role that the dispersive stress plays

tspan.tspan: in the velocity profile. Setting
λ
removes the agreement entirely. This gap is itself a
result: it indicates the importance of the dispersive stress in the momentum balance.

text.tspan: - Nikora, Vladimir et al. “Spatially Averaged Open-Channel Flow over Rough Bed”.
In: Journal of Hydraulic Engineering 127.2 (2001), pp. 123–133. doi: 10.1061/
- Rousseau, G. and C. Ancey. “An experimental investigation of turbulent free-surface flows over a
steep permeable bed”. In: Journal of Fluid Mechanics 941 (2022), A51. doi: 10.1017/jfm.2022.310.

tspan.tspan: The next step is to solve the equation analytically. We will examine the same equation by
deriving matched asymptotic expansions, with distinct inner and outer regions within and
above the bed. This approach aims to obtain an approximate velocity profile and reveal the

text.tspan: parameter groupings that the numerical solution cannot.
